newsitem.title: USA: Fed official cites reluctance to raise prices.
newsitem.headline: Fed official cites reluctance to raise prices.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Governor Laurence Meyer said in an interview with the Washington Post that businesses were reluctant to raise prices.

"There is a new business paradigm: You can't, or think it would be risky to, raise prices," Meyer said. "Maybe you have to hire entry-level employees and pay them more, but you then find offsets and perhaps even increase your profit margins."
"If you are willing to stick at (aninflation rate of)5.5 percent and take your chances, do you stick at five percent and take your chances?," Meyer asked.
The new economic environment "gives you a little more room but it doesn't give you license... We don't want to allow backsliding on inflation," he said.
Another Fed fovernor, Janet Yellen, told the Post that she was not sure she wanted to experiment with a jobless rate noticeably below 5.5 percent because it might boost inflation.
The Fed is to meet on Sept. 24 to consider whether to raise short-term interest rates amid conflicting signs from the economy with consumer spending tapering off and strong increases in employement.
